name: Hindustan Media Ventures Ltd
title: Hindustan Media Ventures Ltd - 533217 - Announcement under Regulation 30 (LODR)-Earnings Call Transcript

read.thesis: Consolidated revenue up 15% to INR 497 crore and EBITDA near 3x to INR 90 crore, but the quarter is flattered by treasury and asset-sale gains, digital is shrinking, and a below-book preferential issue is dilutive to minority holders.

summary.headline: HMVL Q1 FY27: consolidated revenue up 15% to INR 497 crore and EBITDA nearly 3x to INR 90 crore, while a preferential equity issue at ~INR 24.7 drew shareholder pushback.
summary.overview: Consolidated revenue rose 15% YoY to INR 497 crore, with EBITDA up nearly 3x to INR 90 crore (margin up 12 points) and PAT of INR 47 crore (9% margin). Print drove growth, with advertising up 15% to INR 295 crore and operating revenue up 16% to INR 376 crore, while Digital revenue fell about 28% and Radio stayed flat with negative EBITDA. Management also announced a preferential issue at the SEBI-formula price (~INR 24.7 per share) in HT Media and Digicontent Ltd, not HMVL, to retire 30-50% of debt; this drew sharp objections from minority shareholders on dilution and pricing. Treasury gains and asset-sale profit lifted other income in HMVL.

financial_highlights.change: +12% YoY; sequential decline attributed to seasonality
operating EBITDA negative INR 3 crore; margin -12%
from INR 111 crore a year ago

segments.name: Print
segments.commentary: Advertising up 15% to INR 295 crore and operating revenue up 16% to INR 376 crore, with EBITDA margin of 13% despite high newsprint costs. Growth attributed mainly to yield (pricing) improvement in commercial, plus government rate hike from November 2025.

segments.name: Radio
segments.commentary: Topline flat YoY with negative operating EBITDA of INR 3 crore. Company surrendered licences for certain non-viable stations to run a leaner footprint.

segments.name: Digital
segments.commentary: Operating revenue down about 28% and operating EBITDA negative INR 3 crore (margin -12%), reflecting a deliberate portfolio reset toward leaner offerings.

segments.name: OTTplay / incubating businesses
segments.commentary: Management said a decision on OTTplay was taken around 31 March 2026, and incubating businesses that do not turn profitable will be reviewed; no figures were disclosed for the discontinued operations.

guidance_outlook: No formal revenue or earnings guidance given; management said it does forward planning but is 'very hopeful' of sustaining current numbers.

Newsprint (25-40% of print bill of material) at about USD 650-700 per metric ton, seen as a peak that should plateau; management said 13% Print EBITDA margin can be used as a modelling baseline if prices and USD do not worsen.
Q2 FY27 newsprint price slightly higher than Q1; margin outcome depends on ad category mix and pricing.
Government revenue rate increase (November 2025) will continue to support the next two quarters as prior-year pricing is lapped.
Preferential issue proceeds expected to retire at least 30-50% of HT Media/DCL debt, described as EPS-accretive and supportive of interest coverage and credit rating.
capex_capacity: Radio surrendered licences for certain non-viable stations, moving to a leaner footprint.
No capex or capacity figures were disclosed in the call.
demand_pricing: Commercial ad revenue: volumes held and yield improved; yield improvement programme cited as a key driver.
Government ad revenue grew on a combination of volume and pricing after the November 2025 rate hike (first in seven years).
English circulation revenue (INR 13 crore, +14%) driven mainly by pricing and mix; copy levels described as steady state.
Cover price hikes seen as difficult: Hindi papers already well priced, and most peers have taken increases.
Newsprint has no forward market, and a stronger USD (at a lifetime high) adds to cost pressure.

qa_highlights.question: Ranga Prasad: why raise equity via a preferential issue at ~INR 24 when net cash is INR 922 crore, diluting public shareholders by 15%, and why not a rights issue? Asked for withdrawal.
qa_highlights.answer: Piyush Gupta said net cash sits in HMVL, while HT Media and Digicontent are net debt companies; the issue is priced on the SEBI formula (higher of 10-day or 90-day VWAP) with no premium, and P/B is below 0.5. Anna Abraham said a preferential issue is faster (2-3 months) and gives more certainty than a rights issue, which carries underwriting and under-subscription risk.

qa_highlights.question: Mehul Pathak: the issue price is unjustifiably low versus book value and intrinsic value; ROE is under 10% even at current profits, and other options should be considered.
qa_highlights.answer: Gupta said the market values HMVL at about one-third of book, the promoter is subscribing on the same terms, and all options (including OTTplay decision) are being discussed at Board level. Pathak said he voted against the resolution.

qa_highlights.question: Mehul Pathak: management previously said the company was debt free and used debt only for treasury, but now debt is being retired.
qa_highlights.answer: Gupta said HT Media has carried debt for three to four years, built up post-COVID from English Print and Radio operations, and that the combined net cash figure hides this.

qa_highlights.question: Rohan Agarwal: what is the nature of the other income jump at HMVL?
qa_highlights.answer: Anna Abraham said it comprised treasury gains (mutual fund NAV-based, driven by yield curve movement at quarter end) and realised profit on sale of assets; no MTM on equity investments. Future levels cannot be predicted.

qa_highlights.question: Rohan Agarwal: outlook for newsprint costs, hedging, and whether the 13% Print margin is a baseline; would cover price hikes help?
qa_highlights.answer: Gupta said newsprint is 25-40% of costs, peaked near USD 650-700/MT, and there is no forward market; 13% margin can be used as a model baseline. Anna Abraham said Q2 newsprint is slightly higher and cover price hikes are difficult given existing hikes.

qa_highlights.question: Yash R.: what drove 15% Print ad growth, and what was the government share of revenue?
qa_highlights.answer: Anna Abraham said commercial volumes held with yield gains and government revenue grew on volume and pricing. Gupta said growth was largely pricing-driven; government share is 'substantial' but not disclosed, with commercial the bigger block.

qa_highlights.question: Yash R.: why did consolidated employee cost fall and other operating income rise at HMVL?
qa_highlights.answer: Gupta attributed lower employee cost (about INR 99 crore vs INR 111 crore) to right-sizing across HT Media and HMVL. Anna Abraham said other operating income (job work, scrap sales) roughly doubled to about INR 20 crore.

risks_watch: Preferential issue at SEBI-formula price (~INR 24.7) to HT Media and Digicontent: shareholder vote and pricing objections from minority holders; at least 30-50% of HT Media/DCL debt to be retired from proceeds.
Newsprint (25-40% of Print bill of material) at a peak of about USD 650-700/MT with no forward market; Q2 FY27 newsprint slightly higher than Q1, and a strong USD adds cost pressure.

Sustainability of the 13% Print EBITDA margin and 15% Print advertising growth, which management attributes mainly to yield; government rate hike support lapses after the next two quarters as prior-year pricing is lapped.
Other income quality: treasury gains depend on yield curve movement and realised profit on asset sales; management said future levels cannot be predicted.

Digital (operating revenue down about 28%, EBITDA negative INR 3 crore) and Radio (negative EBITDA INR 3 crore) remain loss-making; OTTplay and other incubating businesses under review, with no figures disclosed.
Capital allocation and disclosure: low ROE (under 10% per analyst), the debt build-up in HT Media versus earlier debt-free statements, and how HMVL's surplus cash will be deployed.
key_quotes: We have a very substantially healthy balance sheet position with net cash at INR 922 crores. But you have to understand that all that cash is parked in HMVL.
At least 30 % to 50% of the debt will be retired, which will definitely be accretive to the EPS and long-term interest coverage ratio, our credit rating and so on and so forth.
So, a substantial part of that revenue growth of 15% is driven by our pricing .
We believe that the prices have peaked and should plateau at this level before they start coming down. But obviously, as a commodity, no one can predict, that's our best estimate.
summary.management_tone: Confident on operating performance, pricing/yield and cost discipline, but defensive and evasive on the preferential issue, the debt history and capital allocation; management declined to give guidance and repeatedly deflected pricing and dilution questions to the SEBI formula and to the separate HMVL board.

growth.why: No formal revenue or earnings guidance was given; management said it is 'very hopeful' of sustaining current numbers, with Print growth driven by yield/pricing and a government rate hike lapping over the next two quarters, but no capacity or order figures back it.
